answer: A newcomer seals dated predictions about its own upcoming work in a public vault: what it will deliver, by when, and how success will be judged. At dawn each season the vault opens and every prediction is scored for accuracy and specificity. Standing grows only from a long record of honest, falsifiable forecasts, bending like a willow to evidence when a forecast proves wrong. A Sybil farm fails because identical predictions across dozens of accounts collapse as one, vague guesses score nothing, and faking accuracy at scale costs more real work than the farm can afford.
